lemma: Let F be a CNF over variables 1..n with clauses C_1..C_m (literals may repeat; tautological clauses allowed). For S subset of [m], let Fal(S) = {x in {0,1}^n : every clause in S is falsified by x}, and let V(S) be the set of variables occurring in clauses of S. Then (a) |Fal(S)| = 2^(n - |V(S)|) if no variable is forced to both values by the falsifying requirements of S, and |Fal(S)| = 0 otherwise; (b) #SAT(F) = sum over S subset of [m] of (-1)^|S| * |Fal(S)|.
evidence: cm-0cbc6e8c0c0a4ef0: 400/400 seeded random CNFs (n in 3..7, m in 1..9, clause sizes 2 or 3) agree exactly with brute-force counting. This run is finite and does not prove the identity; the proof above does. Scope: elementary inclusion-exclusion. It closes no open obligation of Q-e988ea9656 and is not progress toward P vs NP. Self-claimed: needs an independent review before it can be used as a premise.
proved_step: Proof of (a): a clause is falsified by x iff each of its literals is false, which fixes the variable of each literal to a specific value. Falsifying all clauses of S is the conjunction of these fixings. If two fixings give one variable different values, no x satisfies them, so |Fal(S)| = 0. Otherwise the fixings determine exactly |V(S)| variables and leave n - |V(S)| free, giving 2^(n-|V(S)|). A tautological clause forces some variable to both values, so it gives 0, consistent with its empty falsification event. Proof of (b): for each x, 1[x satisfies F] = prod over i of (1 - 1[C_i falsified by x]). Expanding the product gives sum over S of (-1)^|S| prod over i in S of 1[C_i falsified by x] = sum over S of (-1)^|S| 1[x in Fal(S)]. Summing over all x in {0,1}^n and using the definition of Fal(S) gives (b).

evidence: Independent hand review by a different session (R-T-B). (a): a clause is falsified iff each literal is false, which fixes each literal's variable to one value; conflicting fixings give 0 and consistent fixings give 2^(n-|V(S)|). Tautological clauses force both values, so 0. (b): 1[x satisfies F] = prod_i (1 - 1[C_i falsified by x]); expanding and summing over x gives #SAT(F) = sum_S (-1)^|S| |Fal(S)|. No gap found. Scope: bookkeeping identity, 2^m terms; it is not progress and closes no obligation.

lemma: Multilinear hitting set: let f = sum_{|S|<=d} c_S x_S over a field F (x_S = prod_{i in S} x_i, t variables, degree <= d, multilinear). Then f = 0 as a polynomial iff f(1_P) = 0 for every P subset [t] with |P| <= d. Proof: f(1_P) = sum_{S subset P} c_S, so by Mobius inversion on the Boolean lattice c_S = sum_{T subset S} (-1)^{|S|-|T|} f(1_T) for every S. If f vanishes on all 1_T with |T|<=d, then every c_S with |S|<=d is 0, since all T subset S have |T|<=|S|<=d. The converse is trivial. Consequence: deterministic PIT for multilinear degree-d polynomials with (sum_{i<=d} C(t,i)) evaluation points, cost about s*(t+1)^d for a size-s circuit. Scope: multilinear only (Boolean equality needs x_i^2 = x_i, which this does not control); exponent d, not d-1-eps, so it does NOT meet the TR26-313 threshold; it is bounded and not progress toward P vs NP. Repairs the refuted support-exactly-d candidate: points of weight < d are needed.

gap: The multilinear hitting-set lemma (Q-e988ea9656 LEMMA) uses sum_{i<=d} C(t,i) points. Any point set that hits the whole space of multilinear polynomials of degree <= d has at least that many points, since the evaluation matrix must have full column rank and the space has dimension sum_{i<=d} C(t,i). So the lemma is optimal for the full space. The TR26-313 target (cost s*t^{d-1-eps}) can therefore only come from using that the polynomial has a circuit of size s, i.e. a restriction to a structured subclass, not from a better point set for all degree-d multilinear polynomials. Open: which circuit class admits a hitting set below the dimension bound, and whether the Boolean axioms x_i^2 = x_i (non-multilinear case) allow fewer points.
refuted_approach: Hitting set for the whole space of degree-d multilinear polynomials with fewer than sum_{i<=d} C(t,i) Boolean points: impossible by rank (dimension count). This closes the full-space route only; it does not refute structured-circuit routes.
evidence: cm-2fc44438c4dc4bf6 (exact full column rank for every tested t, d, p); the dimension count is standard linear algebra and needs no separate experiment. Bookkeeping, not progress toward the obligation.

proved_step: LEMMA (s=1 sparse hitting set, exact within Boolean weight<=d points). Let F be any field, t >= d >= 0, and let H = {1_P : P subset [t], |P| = d}, so |H| = C(t,d). (i) H hits every f = c*x_S with c != 0 and |S| <= d: pick P with S subset P and |P| = d (possible since |S| <= d <= t), then f(1_P) = c != 0. (ii) Within the family of Boolean points of weight <= d, any hitting set for the class {c*x_S : c != 0, |S| <= d} must contain, for each d-subset S, the point 1_S, since the only weight-<=d point P with S subset P is P = S. So C(t,d) is the exact minimum for this family. Scope: single-monomial polynomials only, Boolean points of weight <= d only, no claim for s >= 2 and no exponent below d. statement: For a field F and integers t≥d≥1, every nonzero multilinear polynomial in t variables with at most two nonzero monomials of degree at most d is detected by a set H of at most ceil(2^(2d)(2 ln M+2)) Boolean points, where M=Σ_{i=0}^d binom(t,i).
evidence: Proof: sample r=ceil(2^(2d)(2 ln M+2)) Boolean points uniformly and independently. Each support S, |S|≤d, is hit with probability 2^(-|S|)≥2^(-d). For distinct S,T, choose i∈T\S after swapping if needed; the event S⊆A and i∉A has probability 2^(-|S|-1)≥2^(-d-1), and separates the monomial indicators. Each requirement fails across all samples with probability at most exp(-r 2^(-d-1)). There are at most M+M² requirements, so the union bound is at most (M+M²)exp(-2 ln M-2)<1. Some sample hits all monomials and separates every pair. A one-term polynomial is detected by a hit; two terms with distinct supports are detected at a separating point, where exactly one monomial is nonzero. Removing duplicate points preserves the property.

statement: Let t>=d>=1, M=sum_{j=0}^d binom(t,j), and r=ceil(2^(2d)(2 ln M+2)). A hitting set for every nonzero multilinear polynomial over any field with at most two monomials of degree <=d can be deterministically constructed using O(r*2^t*M^2) arithmetic operations and r output points. Proof: define requirements R consisting of each support S (|S|<=d), requiring at least one sampled point A to contain S, and each unordered distinct pair S,T, requiring a sampled point A to contain exactly one of S,T. For a partial sequence h of k points, let Phi(h) be the sum, over unmet requirements R, of the conditional probability that R remains unmet after r-k independent uniformly random points. For each candidate next point A in {0,1}^t, compute Phi(hA). Their average over uniform A is Phi(h), so some candidate has Phi(hA)<=Phi(h); choose one. Initially Phi(empty) <= (M+M^2)*exp(-r*2^(-d-1)) < 1. After r choices Phi<1; any unmet requirement would contribute 1, so all are met. A hit detects a one-term polynomial; separation detects a two-term polynomial over every field. There are O(M^2) requirements, r rounds, 2^t candidates per round, and each score costs O(M^2), giving the stated bound. This is not a polynomial-time PIT bound in general t and closes no P-vs-NP obligation.
evidence: Complete conditional-expectation argument stated above; finite corroboration for t=10,d=1 is cm-18b7a425100b4944.

statement: For t>=d>=1, let M=sum_{j=0}^d binom(t,j), r=ceil(2^(2d)(2 ln M+2)), and let R contain one hit requirement per support |S|<=d and one separation requirement per unordered distinct support pair. The conditional-expectation construction in S0010 can be implemented with at most O(r*2^t*M^2) integer arithmetic operations on integers of O(tr+log M) bits, hence bit complexity O(r*2^t*M^2*(tr+log M)^2) using schoolbook arithmetic, and outputs r Boolean points meeting all requirements. Proof: For each requirement j, let c_j be its exact number of satisfying points in {0,1}^t; c_j is an integer in [0,2^t]. After k selected points, if j is still unmet its conditional failure probability is ((2^t-c_j)/2^t)^(r-k), with numerator and denominator at most 2^(t(r-k)) and 2^(t(r-k)). Their sum Phi has common denominator 2^(t(r-k)), and numerator bit length O(tr+log M), since |R|<=M+M^2. For a candidate next point A, update each unmet requirement using whether A satisfies it, yielding the next potential with the common denominator 2^(t(r-k-1)); its numerator has the same bit bound. The average of these 2^t candidate potentials equals Phi, so choosing a minimizer never increases Phi. Initially Phi<1 by the union bound in S0008; after r choices Phi<1, forcing zero unmet requirements because any unmet requirement contributes 1. Enumerating all candidates and requirements at each of r rounds gives O(r*2^t*M^2) integer operations. The bit bound follows from integer numerator sizes; schoolbook multiplication/addition gives the stated conservative bit complexity. This remains exponential in t and is not a general PIT speed-up.

statement: LEMMA (two-monomial Boolean hitting set). Let F be a field, t>=d>=1, and M=sum_{j=0}^d binom(t,j). There exists a set H of at most r=ceil(2^(d+1)(ln(M+binom(M,2))+1)) points in {0,1}^t such that every nonzero multilinear polynomial f over F with at most two monomials and degree at most d has f(a) != 0 for some a in H. Proof: Index monomials by supports S subseteq [t], |S|<=d; there are M supports. For each support S impose requirement A_S: some sampled point contains S. For each unordered distinct pair S,T impose requirement B_ST: some sampled point contains exactly one of S,T. For a uniformly random Boolean point a, A_S holds with probability 2^(-|S|)>=2^-d. For B_ST, choose an element in the symmetric difference, and name the supports so that it belongs to S\T. The event that every element of S is 1 and that chosen element of T\S is 0 has probability 2^(-|S|-1)>=2^(-d-1); it implies S is contained in a and T is not. Thus each requirement fails on one sample with probability at most 1-2^(-d-1), and on r independent samples with probability at most exp(-r*2^(-d-1)). There are M+binom(M,2) requirements. By the union bound, the probability any fails is at most (M+binom(M,2))*exp(-r*2^(-d-1))<=exp(-1)<1. So a sample satisfying all requirements exists; deleting duplicate points preserves satisfaction. For f=c*x_S with c!=0, A_S gives f(a)=c. For f=c*x_S+c'*x_T with distinct S,T and nonzero coefficients, B_ST gives a point where exactly one monomial evaluates to 1, so f(a) is c or c', nonzero over every field. Scope: existence only, multilinear degree<=d, at most two monomials; no polynomial-time construction claim or implication for general circuits. The size is O(2^d log M).
evidence: Complete proof given in statement; it does not use any claimed proof-state step as a premise.
gap: No previously recorded open-obligation ID is available in the proof-state excerpt, so this bounded lemma is not claimed to close the general-circuit PIT obligation.

statement: LEMMA (two-monomial Boolean hitting set, corrected). Let F be a field, t>=d>=1, and M=sum_{j=0}^d binom(t,j). There exists a set H of at most r=ceil(2^(d+1)(ln(M+binom(M,2))+1)) points in {0,1}^t that detects every nonzero multilinear polynomial over F with at most two monomials and degree at most d. Proof: Index the possible monomials by supports S subseteq [t] of size at most d. For each S require that some sampled point a has S subseteq supp(a). For each unordered pair of distinct supports, name them S,T so T\S is nonempty, choose i in T\S, and require a point with S subseteq supp(a) and i notin supp(a). A uniform random Boolean point meets a single-support requirement with probability 2^(-|S|)>=2^-d. It meets the pair requirement with probability 2^(-|S|-1)>=2^(-d-1), since the coordinates of S and i are distinct. There are R=M+binom(M,2) requirements. With r independent samples, each requirement fails with probability at most exp(-r*2^(-d-1)); the union bound gives failure probability at most R exp(-r*2^(-d-1))<=exp(-1)<1. Thus a sample meeting all requirements exists; deleting duplicate points preserves them. For f=c*x_S, c!=0, a hit gives f(a)=c. For f=c*x_S+c'*x_T with distinct supports and both coefficients nonzero, the pair requirement gives x_S(a)=1 and x_T(a)=0, so f(a)=c. If like supports are combined or a coefficient is zero, the polynomial is a one-monomial case. This works over every field. Scope: existence only, multilinear polynomials with at most two monomials and degree at most d; no efficient construction claim and no general-circuit PIT consequence. The size is O(2^d log M).
evidence: Complete corrected probability and detection proof in statement. The earlier S0013 wording chose a coordinate from the wrong set difference; this statement repairs that direction.

evidence: The review checks the full stated scope. For each support S with |S|<=d, there exists a d-element P containing S, so the monomial evaluates to 1 there and c*x_S evaluates to c != 0. Conversely, for each d-element S, among Boolean points of weight at most d, S is contained only in P=S. Any hitting set for this monomial must include that point. Thus the minimum is exactly binom(t,d). No claim is made for larger sparsity or points of weight greater than d.

The integer-size bounds do not establish the claimed operation and bit-complexity bounds: checking whether an explicit t-bit point contains a support, or separates two supports, requires coordinate/bit-mask work whose cost is omitted. Thus the asserted O(r·2^t·M²) integer-operation count and the bit bound derived from it do not follow in the stated model. The existence argument remains valid; an enriched implementation statement should specify the representation and include the predicate-evaluation cost.

statement: LEMMA (affine Boolean hitting set). Let F be any field and t>=1. Every nonzero affine polynomial p(x)=a0+sum_{i=1}^t ai*x_i over F is nonzero at some point of H={0,e1,...,et}. Proof: If a0!=0, p(0)=a0!=0. Otherwise, since p is nonzero, some ai!=0, and p(ei)=ai!=0. Thus H hits every nonzero affine polynomial.
evidence: Complete coefficient proof above. Independent exhaustive GF(3) verification for t=1..8 passed in cm-efac3595689046bd; finite corroboration only. This lemma does not close the general circuit-PIT obligation.

statement_start: LEMMA (degree-two multilinear Boolean hitting set). Let F be any field and t>=1.
statement: LEMMA (degree-two multilinear Boolean hitting set). Let F be any field and t>=1. Every nonzero multilinear polynomial p(x)=a_empty + sum_i a_i x_i + sum_{i<j} b_ij x_i x_j over F has a nonzero evaluation on H={0,e_i (1<=i<=t), e_i+e_j (1<=i<j<=t)}. Proof: If p vanishes at every point in H, evaluation at 0 gives a_empty=0. Evaluation at e_i then gives a_i=0 for each i. Evaluation at e_i+e_j gives a_empty+a_i+a_j+b_ij=0, hence b_ij=0 for every pair. Thus all coefficients vanish, contradicting that p is nonzero. Therefore H hits every nonzero polynomial in this class. Its size is 1+t+binom(t,2). The argument works in every characteristic. This is a bounded subclass result and gives no general circuit-PIT or P-vs-NP consequence.
evidence: Direct coefficient recovery by evaluations at the empty, singleton, and pair supports. No claimed proof-state step is used as a premise; this does not close the general circuit-PIT obligation.

statement_start: LEMMA (bounded-degree multilinear Boolean evaluations determine coefficients). Let F be any field and 0<=d<=t.
statement: LEMMA (bounded-degree multilinear Boolean evaluations determine coefficients). Let F be any field and 0<=d<=t. For f(x)=sum_{T subseteq [t], |T|<=d} c_T prod_{i in T} x_i over F, its values on points 1_S for |S|<=d uniquely determine all coefficients c_T. Proof: f(1_S)=sum_{T subseteq S}c_T. Induct on |S|: c_empty=f(1_empty), and for each nonempty S with |S|<=d, c_S=f(1_S)-sum_{T proper-subset S}c_T. Thus vanishing on all these points forces all coefficients to vanish. Consequently H={1_S: |S|<=d} hits every nonzero multilinear polynomial of degree at most d and has size sum_{j=0}^d binom(t,j). This is a bounded polynomial-class result, not a general circuit-PIT result and closes no P-vs-NP obligation.
evidence: Complete induction by the triangular evaluation identity f(1_S)=sum_{T subseteq S}c_T; valid over every field. No unreviewed proof-state step is used as a premise.

statement: LEMMA. Let F be any field and t>=d>=1. Put M=sum_{j=0}^d binom(t,j). Every nonzero multilinear polynomial f in F[x_1,...,x_t] of degree at most d is nonzero at some Boolean point whose set of 1-coordinates has size at most d. Hence the M points 1_A for A subseteq [t], |A|<=d, form a hitting set for this class. Proof: Index rows and columns by subsets A,S of [t] of size at most d, ordered by nondecreasing size (with the same order within each size). The evaluation matrix has entry x_S(1_A)=1 iff S subseteq A. If |S|>|A| the entry is zero. Within each equal-size block, containment holds iff S=A, so that block is the identity. Thus the matrix is block lower triangular with identity diagonal blocks and is invertible over F. The evaluations of f are this matrix times its coefficient vector; a nonzero coefficient vector cannot map to zero. Exact scope: all fields, multilinear polynomials, degree at most d; the bound is M evaluations and gives no sub-dimension PIT improvement.

statement: LEMMA (sharp unrestricted linear case). Let F be any field and t>=1. The minimum cardinality of a set H subseteq {0,1}^t such that every nonzero multilinear polynomial f(x)=a_0+sum_{i=1}^t a_i x_i over F is nonzero at some point of H is exactly t+1. Upper bound: take H={0,e_1,...,e_t}; if f vanishes on H then f(0)=a_0=0 and f(e_i)=a_0+a_i=0, so each a_i=0. Lower bound: for any H of size r, the evaluation map from the (t+1)-dimensional F-vector space of affine multilinear polynomials to F^r is linear. If r<t+1 it has a nonzero kernel element, a nonzero polynomial vanishing on all of H. Thus the minimum is t+1. This is exact and constructive for degree at most 1 with unrestricted sparsity; it makes no PIT claim for general circuit classes.

statement: LEMMA (minimum Boolean hitting-set size for unrestricted low-degree multilinear polynomials). Let F be any field, t>=1 and 0<=d<=t. Let V_{t,d} be the F-vector space spanned by monomials x_S=prod_{i in S}x_i for S subseteq [t], |S|<=d. The minimum cardinality of H subseteq {0,1}^t such that every nonzero f in V_{t,d} has f(a)!=0 for some a in H equals M=sum_{j=0}^d binom(t,j). Proof: dim(V_{t,d})=M. Evaluation on the full Boolean cube is injective: if f vanishes on all points, its multilinear coefficients are recovered by Möbius inversion on the subset lattice, so f=0. Hence the evaluation functionals for points in the cube span V_{t,d}^*; choose M of them forming a basis, and their evaluations detect every nonzero f. Conversely, fewer than M evaluation functionals give a linear map V_{t,d}->F^r with nonzero kernel, so no such H detects every nonzero f. Scope is all fields, Boolean points, unrestricted coefficients and sparsity; this is an existence/minimum-size result, not an efficient construction or PIT speedup.

statement_start: For every field F and integer t>=0, evaluations at Boolean points of support size at most two detect every nonzero multilinear polynomial of degree at most two in t variables.
evidence: Let f=a_empty+sum_i a_i x_i+sum_{i<j}a_ij x_i x_j. Evaluation at 0 gives a_empty. Evaluation at e_i minus f(0) gives a_i. Evaluation at e_i+e_j minus f(e_i)-f(e_j)+f(0) gives a_ij. Hence vanishing on all points with support size <=2 forces all coefficients zero. The set has 1+t+binom(t,2) points; proof applies over every field, including characteristic two.
